purpose: Descriptive held-out comparison on a fixed finite benchmark; no population p-values or independent-query standard errors.
freeze_status: Written before the first Study C analysis run; no outcome-dependent query or temperature selection.
partition_rule: numpy.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(1797); first 600 representation, next 40 queries, next 600 reference, remaining 557 evaluation
representation: StandardScaler with training-only mean and population variance, scale 1 for training-constant pixels; PCA(3,svd_solver='full') trained only on the representation set; normalize projected vectors to S2
near_zero_rule: Flag and exclude invalid reference/evaluation vectors without replacement; invalid query gets an explicit failure record. Record all IDs.
weight_rule: exp(beta*cosine(standardized 64-dimensional query, standardized 64-dimensional observation)); normalize within reference and evaluation pools separately
fit: Unpenalized common fit_dual engine; no ridge, moment shrinkage, gap clipping, or significance calculation
evaluation: Normalized evaluation weights times log p_FisherBingham minus log p_vMF, in nats; retain negative values
descriptive_comparators: model curvature score multiplied by reference sample count
association: Spearman rank correlation only, without p-values, for every comparator versus held-out gain across all 40 queries
decision: For each comparator rank all queries by its reference-only value; select the largest half (20), ties by fixed query order. Report total gain divided by all 40 queries, selected mean gain, and negative-gain counts. Include always-vMF and always-FisherBingham policies; this is a fixed budget comparison, not learned deployment policy.
low_first_order: Report lower I1 quartile (10 queries) defined from the reference fit alone, along with all-query results
scope: Representation is a constructed scientific target. Shared fit/evaluation pools make query summaries dependent. Writer IDs are unavailable in load_digits. Labels describe queries and do not set geometric adequacy. No claim of benchmark-wide or population superiority.
